transcript:
Meeting header: POC weekly caching sync
Date: 2025-07-08
Start time: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Kim (Redwood SE), Jasmine Lee (Stratus CTO), Carlos Mendez (ML Eng), Priya Rao (Product), Ethan Wu (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Reviewed last 7-day cache telemetry. Prefix cache hit rate improved after prompt cleaning but KV hit rate still low for multi-turn flows. Agreed on canonicalization rules, TTL tweaks, and 24h follow-up test.

[00:00] Samir: hey team, thanks for hopping on, uh quick check in on the caching POC. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jasmine: good, thanks. we pulled the latest config you sent last week and ran it against our staging traffic for three days.
[00:12] Carlos: yeah i can share numbers in a sec, but short version, prefix cache hit rate moved from about 22% to 38% after we normalized prompts, but KV cache for multi-turn is still only around 9%.
[00:24] Leah: okay that's useful — thanks carlos. did you apply the canonicalization rules Samir suggested (trim, lowercase, remove session ids)?
[00:31] Carlos: mostly yes. we missed stripping some tracking params, that might explain the variance.
[00:36] Priya: also noticed that some product prompts include user-specific tokens, so reuse is low unless we rewrite them.
[00:43] Samir: right, prompt reuse strategy is key. for prefix cache we expect good gains when the prompt prefix is stable; for KV cache we need stable conversation keys. two parallel levers: canonicalize prefixes and create conversation hashing that ignores ephemeral tokens.
[00:58] Ethan: quick infra question — what's the memory footprint of the KV cache at current size? we're on a single dedicated node for the POC.
[01:05] Leah: current config keeps ~200k entries, estimated memory around 12GB including kv meta, but we can tune eviction to LRU with a target of 10GB to fit your node.
[01:14] Jasmine: from a security perspective we also want to confirm that cached items are encrypted at rest and that retention can be limited for PII.
[01:21] Samir: absolutely — cached blobs are stored encrypted in the Redwood-managed cache when hosted; for your private deployment we'll hand off KMS controls. we documented retention TTLs in the security packet — i'll resend.
[01:32] Carlos: returning to hit rates, the breakdown i have: prefix hits 38%, KV hits 9%, overall token savings ~12%, average latency per request improved by ~30ms on cache hits. i can paste the sheet later.
[01:47] Leah: thanks. two thoughts: 1) incrementally increase prefix match threshold (i.e., normalize more aggressively) and 2) change KV keying to use conversation fingerprint that strips out ephemeral entities. both are low-risk experiments.
[02:00] Priya: what's the tradeoff for over-normalizing? we don't want to collapse different intents into the same key.
[02:08] Samir: good point — the canonicalization should be intent-aware when possible. heuristics: remove session ids, user ids, timestamps, but keep verbs and entity placeholders. we can also compute a lightweight intent hash from intent classifier if you want a safer grouping.
[02:26] Carlos: we don't have an intent classifier in prod yet, that'll be more work. can heuristics get us most of the wins?
[02:32] Leah: yes heuristics typically get 60-80% of potential gain; the rest needs semantic hashing. for the POC i'd do heuristics first.
[02:40] Samir: agreed. also TTL: your current TTL is 48 hours; given your traffic pattern we suggest 24h for higher reuse and smaller memory footprint, then observe. you can bump to 48h if cold-start rates are high.
[02:55] Ethan: eviction policy — LRU vs LFU? what do you recommend for chatty, repeated prompts?
[03:02] Leah: LRU usually works well for conversational workloads with bursts. if you have many long-tail prompts, LFU can help, but requires more bookkeeping. start with LRU.
[03:12] Jasmine: any recommended metrics we should watch day-to-day?
[03:15] Samir: hit rate (prefix and kv), cacheable request ratio, average latency of cache-hit vs miss, memory utilization, and cold-start rate. we've added these to the dashboard we shared.
[03:27] Carlos: i pulled a couple of timing percentiles: p50 latency on hits 80ms, p95 160ms; misses p50 210ms, p95 420ms. so big delta at tail.
[03:40] Leah: that aligns with expectations. one optimization we can try is asynchronous prefetching for likely next-turn keys—prefetching increases throughput but adds complexity.
[03:48] Priya: how safe is prefetching from a cost perspective? if we prefetch too much we could increase tokens served.
[03:53] Samir: true — prefetch needs to be conservative. you can cap prefetch budget as a percentage of traffic or token budget. it often helps UX without a lot of cost if tuned.
[04:03] Carlos: another data point: we saw a bunch of near-duplicates because of trailing punctuation and emojis. should we normalize punctuation?
[04:09] Leah: yes strip trailing punctuation and normalize unicode. emojis can be mapped to textual tokens or stripped based on your use case.
[04:16] Jasmine: legal asked about audit logs for cached reads and writes, is that available?
[04:20] Samir: yes we emit cache events into the audit pipeline; we can filter to the tenant. i'll attach the audit schema with the config.
[04:27] Ethan: with the changes, what's the expected hit rate? if we go aggressive on canonicalization, where do you see KV hit rates going?
[04:34] Leah: heuristics alone we'd expect KV hit rate to increase from 9% to 18-25% in many cases; combined with prefix improvements you could see overall token savings move from 12% to 20-30%. results vary by prompt churn.
[04:47] Priya: that's promising. Carlos, can you run a 24-hour experiment with: full canonicalization rules (strip tracking ids, punctuation, unicode normalize), TTL 24h, LRU eviction, and KV key hashing that strips ephemeral tokens?
[04:58] Carlos: yes i can run that starting tonight. i'll enable the debug logs for hits and misses.
[05:03] Samir: great — next step i will push an updated config and a revised benchmark sheet (with suggested metrics) after the call. also leah will prep a short perf deep-dive once we have the 24h run.
[05:13] Jasmine: timeline looks good. any blockers on your side, redwood?
[05:16] Samir: none on our side. we'll also include recommended kernel selection notes for longer sequences — leah will add that to the deep-dive.
[05:24] Leah: quick note — if you decide to move to a private deployment later, we can provide the same cache semantics; you just run the cache within your VPC with KMS.
[05:33] Priya: perfect. last thing: can you share the sample curl and the staging config we used?
[05:37] Samir: yes i'll send both after the call, plus the security packet on retention and encryption.
[05:42] Jasmine: ok thanks everyone.
[05:44] Samir: cool, we'll follow up with the artifacts. thanks all.

Meeting recap (auto): 1) Customer to run 24h canonicalization + TTL=24h test; 2) Redwood to share updated config and benchmark sheet; 3) Perf deep-dive scheduled after test.

References: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/stratus-caching-2025-07), staging config (link: https://redwood.app/configs/stratus-staging-caching.json), security packet (link: https://redwood.app/security/retention-kms.pdf)
